genZNote: Birds keep the virus circulating in the background all year — humans and horses are basically bystanders who happen to get bitten too.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Maintained in a bird-mosquito-bird transmission cycle
habitat.hostAssociation: Birds serve as the amplifying reservoir host; Culex mosquitoes are the primary vector; humans and horses are incidental, dead-end hosts
habitat.reservoir: Wild birds, with Culex mosquitoes as the vector

identificationClues: Diagnosed by IgM serology on serum or CSF (the standard approach), since viremia is often brief and low by presentation
Most infections (about 80%) are asymptomatic; a minority develop West Nile fever, and less than 1% develop neuroinvasive disease
Neuroinvasive disease (meningitis, encephalitis, or acute flaccid paralysis) is more common in elderly and immunocompromised patients
Surveillance often tracks bird die-offs (e.g., crows) as a sentinel signal of local virus activity

diseases: West Nile fever — mild febrile illness with headache, myalgia, and rash in a minority of infected individuals

West Nile neuroinvasive disease — meningitis, encephalitis, or acute flaccid paralysis (a poliomyelitis-like syndrome), occurring in less than 1% of infections but with substantial morbidity/mortality, particularly in older adults
clinicalImportance.transmission: Bite of an infected Culex mosquito; rarely via blood transfusion, organ transplantation, or vertical transmission
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Widely established across the United States since its introduction in 1999, with seasonal outbreaks each summer/fall tied to mosquito activity; the most common cause of domestically acquired arboviral neuroinvasive disease in the US
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: IgM serology on serum or CSF is the standard diagnostic approach; blood banks screen donations for West Nile virus given the recognized risk of transfusion-transmitted infection

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Not applicable — diagnosed by IgM serology
examFacts.importantDisease: West Nile neuroinvasive disease — encephalitis/meningitis/flaccid paralysis, especially in the elderly
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: A bird-maintained, Culex-transmitted flavivirus that is the most common cause of domestically acquired arboviral neuroinvasive disease in the United States
